candidates.title: Build due-date reminders from a sheet

demandEvidence.chore: Connect spreadsheet rows with due dates to send reminders.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to connect Google Sheets to my Make scenario using the Search Rows module so I can automate reminders based on due dates stored in a spreadsheet.

ease.reason: A spreadsheet and test dates give a simple starting point; the post reports a Make connection problem, not implementation evidence.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: service professionals may pay for fewer missed due-date reminders; this request proves no payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can search sample rows and draft reminders; actual account access and delivery need permission and testing.

autonomy.reason: A schedule and row search could repeat, but the source documents no working automation and a person should review recipients and dates.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly requests reminders based on spreadsheet due dates, but supplies little frequency or process detail.

candidates.reason: Below threshold (unrounded mean 5.2): Connect spreadsheet rows with due dates to send reminders.

candidates.title: Review stock count differences

demandEvidence.chore: Staff record shelf counts and review differences before stock levels change.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: You create a count, staff record what is actually on the shelf using barcode scanning or manual entry, and you review the differences before any stock levels change.

ease.reason: A small sample count can be compared in a spreadsheet; barcode capture and Shopify integration are not evidenced.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small shop operators may pay for quicker count reconciliation; the discussion establishes no commercial demand.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can compare fictional or operator-supplied count rows; live inventory access and dependable matching remain untested.

autonomy.reason: Software could flag count differences, but staff must verify shelf counts and approve any stock changes as the source describes.

evidence.reason: The excerpt gives a concrete count, recording and review sequence, but no frequency or software capability evidence.

candidates.reason: Below threshold (unrounded mean 4.6): Staff record shelf counts and review differences before stock levels change.

steps.message: Assessed all ten assigned discussion identities. Two concrete chores support bounded but below-threshold experiments. The other excerpts are vague, one-off, showcase-only, or duplicate AI-builder demand, so no eligible post is proposed.
